outcome: Serum thromboxane B(2) to 6-keto prostaglandin F(1a) ratio
cohort: Pregnant Wistar rats were fed either a control or vitamin D deficient diet from pre-pregnancy to delivery.
finding: Maternal vitamin D deficiency in Wistar rats led to increased oxidative stress and an imbalance in vasoconstrictor and vasodilator eicosanoids, specifically a higher thromboxane B2/6-keto prostaglandin F1a ratio, through alterations in the one-carbon cycle.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken on day 20 of gestation.
